approach: Add `check_root_cause_diagnosis(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and register it as one `step!` line in `refusing_check`, right after `check_code_survey`. It applies to a reading with a capability, no question, class `code` or `tests` and at least one behavior criterion, when the request text has a bug-fix word as a whole word. It then requires two criteria: (a) one that says "root cause" and where the wrong output enters or why it is not excluded, and (b) one behavior criterion saying a test fails on the base tree or without the change. Otherwise it refuses and names what is missing. Add a `ROOT_CAUSE_GUIDE` constant and a seventh `READING_RULES` line in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs, composed beside `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE`, so the reader writes both criteria before the gate refuses. Add unit tests in reading.rs, corpus cases in refusal_corpus.rs, a CHANGELOG Fixed entry and a short paragraph in docs/architecture.md. The gate reads only the reading and request, never the repository. Prompt files, records and the decisions page are untouched.

decisions.choice: Fix it at the reading gate with a new `check_*` step in `refusing_check`, not in the decisions page code.
decisions.reason: Both rejected jobs (20261103-201526-t4qv, 20261103-231808-3gkq) moved a filter because the accepted reading never required a diagnosis or a test that fails on the base. The gate is where that reading was accepted, so it is where the class starts. `refusing_check` (reading.rs:3192) is the single entry point and the corpus test enforces one case per step.

rejected.why: That is one instance. The brief puts it out of scope and the candidates are dropped.

rejected.option: Add the rule only as reader prose
rejected.why: The user defaults require mechanism, not prose alone. A prompt-only rule does not refuse a reading that skips it.

decisions.choice: Detect a bug-fix job from the request text with whole-word matches via the existing `has_phrase` (reading.rs:3366): fix/fixes/fixed/fixing, bug(s), wrong, broken, regression, fails/failing, already, and the phrase 'still shows'. Lowercase the text and turn `_` into `x`, as `check_governance_coverage` does.
decisions.reason: The accepted reading specifies detection from request text. It reuses a tested word-boundary helper, so 'prefix', 'fixture' and `fix_x` do not match. It needs no new class in the closed class list.

rejected.why: It would change the closed list and config, and the reader could pick another class and bypass the check.

decisions.choice: The root-cause criterion must contain 'root cause' (or 'root-cause') and one locator word stem: where, enter, originat, why, exclud, because. The test criterion must be of kind behavior, contain fail/fails/failing, and name the base tree, base commit, 'on the base', 'without the change', 'without the fix' or 'before the change'.
decisions.reason: This enforces the two things the introspections asked for (where the wrong items enter and why they are not excluded; a test that fails on the base) with no model call. 'No root cause is needed' has no locator and is refused. The test criterion is not required to say 'passes', so the wording of the request's own bullet 'A test fails without the change and passes with it' is accepted.

rejected.why: The reader writes free text; a template would refuse good readings.

rejected.option: Mechanically require 'real recorded data' in the test criterion
rejected.why: Not decidable from text without false refusals. The reader guide asks for it and the doc comment marks it prose-only.

decisions.choice: Put the guidance in a new constant `ROOT_CAUSE_GUIDE` plus a seventh `READING_RULES` line in briefs.rs, and raise the section-size bound in the brief test.
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 asks for a constant composed beside `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE`. Every reading check has a rule line (the test at briefs.rs:3965 lists them), so a new check without one would drift. The bound `section.len() < 2400` (briefs.rs:3984) was set for six rules and one guide, so it must grow with the second guide. These strings are in briefs.rs, not the budgeted prompt files.

rejected.why: The reader set is 1997 of 2000 tokens and the verifier set 1298 of 1300 (docs/system-facts.md), and the brief puts prompt files out of scope.
The criterion asks for a separate constant, and the survey guide is already about the survey.

decisions.choice: Declare 'expected 8% of newly refused readings' in the check's doc comment, in the CHANGELOG entry and in a unit test of `replay_declaration`.
decisions.reason: The replay holds a job above 10% unless a share is declared (reading.rs:3521-3523, `replay_declaration` at 3953). The existing design-check doc test (refusal_corpus.rs:819) shows the pattern to copy.

The refusal text says exactly which two criteria to add, and `read_for` re-reads once with the refusal as a correction. The replay is declared at 8%, under the 10% hold. demonstrations.method: New unit tests in the `mod tests` of crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs. The first builds `code_reading(&[SURVEY], &[MODIFY_READING])` and sets its criteria to a behavior criterion that only describes the page content ('Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: the page shows only undecided proposals'). With the request 'The page lists proposals that were already decided; fix it' it calls `check_root_cause_diagnosis` and `refusing_check`. It asserts the first refusing check is `check_root_cause_diagnosis` and that the message names both the missing root-cause criterion and the missing criterion that a test fails on the base tree. It then adds a root-cause criterion ('The root cause is named: decided proposals enter the page from the unfiltered proposals list, and the filter does not exclude them') and a behavior criterion ('A named test built from approved and rejected proposals fails on the base tree and passes with the change'), and asserts `Ok(())` from the check and from `check_reading_acceptance`. A third assertion drops only the base-failing criterion and expects a refusal naming only that part.
demonstrations.observes: The refusal message contains the phrases for both missing criteria, the first refusing step name equals 'check_root_cause_diagnosis', and the two-criteria reading is accepted.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree `check_root_cause_diagnosis` does not exist, so the tests do not compile. Without the step! line, `refusing_check` returns None and the symptom-only reading is accepted.

The `Reading` is built directly and passed as an argument, with no double and no logic in the fixture.
